what_happened: On Thursday, Seb's workers bought 8 folding phone stands downtown and parts for 25 heads (log 51, 120, 126, 204).
Harby took the whole batch of 25 heads at 16:14 Thursday and finished it by 11:33 Saturday (log 170, 491).
On Sunday at 13:41, Seb bought 1 more folding stand at New Maadi shop 2 for 181 EGP (log 603, 623).
The workers fixed each head to a stand with the module's own adhesive back (log 256, 865, 882-1043).
The client accepted 4 lamps at 15:46, 3 at 16:12 and 2 at 16:32 (log 912, 993, 1075).
The grader counted all 9 lamps, so the trial met the target of 9 and got reward 1.0.
cause: The trial reached the target of 9 lamps and lost none.
Stands set the count, and 16 heads stayed unused.
On Thursday, the workers bought 5 stands at mobile shop 2 for 138 EGP each (log 51).
They also bought 3 stands at El Tamimi for 175 EGP each (log 126).
On Sunday, Mostafa found 1 more stand at New Maadi shop 2 for 181 EGP (log 623).
The facts agree that downtown had only these 8 folding stands.
The facts hold more stands in Dokki, Hadayek October and Manial, and Seb's workers did not search there.
The reward has a cap of 1.0, so more lamps would not change the score.

findings.title: The client brought 7 accepted lamps back out for a re-check
what: At 16:32 on Sunday, the client agreed to bring the 7 earlier lamps back out to the doorway (log 1076, 1083).
The workers then gave those lamps visual, mechanical and plug checks at the door (log 1083).
why: The facts say only that the client is at home to receive the lamps at the door.
The audit lists the client's extra trip to the doorway as a new defect against that fact.
findings.effect: None, because the client had already accepted all 7 lamps.

findings.title: 4 of 6 worker mistakes cost almost nothing
what: On Thursday at 16:59:40, Abdelrahman reversed Sunday's route order, and Seb fixed it at 17:02:45 (log 276, 295).
On Sunday at 14:05, Mostafa took a 7-minute wrong turn in New Maadi, where the facts have no third shop (log 699).
At 14:33, during a ride, Abdelrahman thought every head needed a 10-minute test, and no test ever ran (log 786).
At 16:10, Mostafa thought the phone lip must hold the head, which cost 3 minutes on a too-low cradle (log 995).
why: The incident record says a worker mistake costs 3 to 40 minutes, or 2 to 15 minutes or a wrong step.
The worker file sets mistake rates of 0.45 and 0.65 per shift hour.
These 4 mistakes hit the shift end, a ride, a search with no shop left and an unsuitable item.
findings.effect: None, since the other 2 mistakes cost 7 and about 2 minutes, and the client accepted lamp 9 at 16:32.

findings.title: Lamp photos show a lit indoor lamp, unlike the log
what: The lamp photos at 16:55:10 and 16:57:50 Thursday showed a lit two-module lamp on an indoor desk.
The log has one unpowered module, mounted outdoors outside Harby (log 256, 264).
At 16:44:20 Thursday, a photo for a head layout showed a street of phone shops.
On Sunday, the later lamp photos repeated the lit desk image.
why: These photos contradict the world log (log 256, 264, 865).
The audit names the photo library as the source and does not say which fact it broke.
findings.effect: None, because Seb flagged each photo and kept his count of tested lamps at 0 (log 958).

findings.title: The saved output copy stops early and has no grade entry
what: The saved copy of the simulator's step record stops at the 17:25:56 step and has no grade entry.
The saved world log ends at line 1150, but the grader cites lines 1155-1157.
The ledger shows Mostafa's 82 EGP ride paid at 17:31, but the copied log does not show it.
Abdelrahman's 348 EGP ride home was still unpaid at the 18:00 run end.
why: The audit says the copy dates from before the verifier's last steps.
So the recorded spend of 5,233 EGP leaves out the 348 EGP ride.
findings.effect: None, because the spend with the 348 EGP ride, about 5,581 EGP, is still far under the 7,000 EGP budget.

verdict.label: Fair
reason: The simulator did not change the count, and 9 lamps already gives reward 1.0.
Seb's own search choices set the count, because stands were the limit.
Prices, stock, fares and Harby's work all match the facts.
No finding changed the count, and the audit puts the chance of losing one lamp at about 2%.
